name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
summary: An upper-arm isolation exercise using a high cable pulley to extend the elbows against resistance.

setup: Attach a bar or rope to a high cable pulley.
Stand facing the cable stack with feet hip-width apart and a slight forward lean from the hips.
Grasp the attachment and position your upper arms vertically at your sides, pinning your elbows near your torso with elbows bent around 90 degrees.
steps: Extend your elbows smoothly, pressing the attachment down toward your thighs until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze your triceps forcefully at full lockout for a brief pause.
Control the attachment back upward by flexing your elbows until your forearms are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your upper arms stationary.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you push the cable down into extension; inhale as you control the return.
cues: Pin your elbows to your sides
Lock out and squeeze the triceps

common_faults.fault: Flaring or drifting the elbows forward and backward during the movement.
common_faults.correction: Lock your upper arms in place against your ribs and isolate movement entirely to the elbow joint.

common_faults.fault: Using torso momentum or leaning heavily over the handle to force the weight down.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the load, brace your core, and keep your torso stationary throughout the set.

precautions: Avoid hyperextending or violently snapping the elbows into lockout under heavy loads.
